biography.plain_text: Luis Oberto Jr., also known as Luis Alfonso Oberto Anselmi, is a Venezuelan financier and lawyer whose career developed in securities trading. He owned the brokerage Unovalores and worked with his brother Ignacio through investment companies. His wider interests have included property in Saint Barthélemy and a collection of Latin American art.

long_biography.plain_text:
Alongside his wife, María Graciela Gill, Venezuelan financier Luis Alfonso Oberto assembled a collection of modern Latin American art. It included Carmen Herrera's Amarillo Dos, a yellow-painted wooden construction made in 1971. The work appeared in the artist's retrospective at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York.

His museum support also extended to permanent collections. A gift through the Museum of Modern Art's Latin American and Caribbean Fund brought Carlos Herrera's photograph Armando Reverón into the museum. He also served on MoMA's International Council, joining its network of international supporters.

confidence.reason: Exhibition publisher and specialist review identify the couple's work; MoMA's own object record and annual membership list establish the gift and council service.
